headline: US formally asked Iraq to close all Iran border crossings except two

sources: Iraqi Deputy PM / Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein, exclusive interview to Al Jazeera, Nov 7
fault_line: Is Iraq a US partner or an Iranian ally -- can Baghdad serve both Washington's blockade and Tehran's friendship at once?

sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- Hussein speaking on the record to Al Jazeera] (1) 'The current circumstances suggest the potential for a renewed war in the region.' (2) Washington has formally requested the closure of all border crossings with Iran, with the exception of two. (3) Iraq lost about $60 billion after oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz were halted; exports have since resumed after understandings reached with Washington and Tehran. (4) Iraq has evidence that external parties have been using Iraqi territory to launch attacks on neighbouring countries; Baghdad is investigating attacks launched from Iraqi territory against Gulf states. (5) Baghdad told Iran it welcomes friendship and an alliance but rejects any interference in Iraq's internal affairs; it is negotiating with Iran-aligned armed factions to bring their weapons under state control through dialogue, not force, and is in contact with Tehran on faction weapons. (6) Baghdad is seeking to resolve disagreements with Saudi Arabia through dialogue. [CONTEXT -- Iraq Oil Minister Basim Mohammed via Reuters/Dawn, Nov 7] Iraq produces more than 5 million barrels/day and is pushing for a higher OPEC quota; oil accounted for 88% of government income last year. [FRANCHISE NOTE] The $60B figure is Hussein's claim, not a counted figure; no new IMF PortWatch snapshot exists (latest Oct 26, observation Oct 18, STALE) -- no counted transit figure is cited. The pre-war '130 ships/day, 20% of global oil' figure is Brig. Gen. Akraminia's claim via IRNA, Nov 7 -- attributed, not counted.
sections.what_verified: 1 distinct publisher family (Al Jazeera) -- the interview itself is the primary source; Kurdistan24 and Dawn relay the same Al Jazeera interview (same underlying source, not independent corroboration). PASS GATE met via primary_source_single_family: the claim IS the actor's own statement.
sections.what_disputed: No US statement confirming the border-closure request has surfaced; CENTCOM's Nov 7 Iron Gate announcement covers US interagency coordination on land/Caspian routes but names no Iraq request. The full interview airs 18:00 GMT Sunday Nov 8 on Al Jazeera -- the on-air version may add or soften wording. Iran has not publicly responded to Hussein's 'no interference' line.
sections.why_matters: America just asked Iraq to seal Iran's land border -- and Baghdad says the blockade already cost it $60 billion.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (Al Jazeera article published 2026-11-07T14:24:48Z = 18:24 ; Kurdistan24 16:13+03 = 17:13 ; Dawn liveblog relay 20:30 PKT = 19:30 ; ZERO 'Fuad Hussein'/'border crossing' mentions in any prior Nov 7 scan -- grep confirms) -- Iraq FM Fuad Hussein to Al Jazeera: US formally asked Iraq to close all Iran border crossings except two; Iraq lost ~$60B from the Hormuz oil halt; exports have resumed; external parties using Iraqi soil to attack neighbours

totw_analysis: Our read: America just asked Iraq to seal Iran's land border -- and Baghdad says the blockade already cost it $60 billion. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is Iraq a US partner or an Iranian ally -- can Baghdad serve both Washington's blockade and Tehran's friendship at once?
